```{r setup, include = FALSE}
NOT_CRAN <- identical(tolower(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN", "false")), "true")
# network chunks need NOT_CRAN and a reachable CPCB feed
CPCB_OK <- NOT_CRAN && tryCatch(
  {
    httr::status_code(httr::HEAD(
      "https://airquality.cpcb.gov.in/caaqms/iit_rss_feed_with_coordinates",
      httr::timeout(5)
    )) < 400
  },
  error = function(e) FALSE
)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 5,
  eval = CPCB_OK
)
```

# Introduction

**vayuayan** (वायुअयन) is an R package that downloads and analyzes air quality data. The data comes from WUSTL ACAG satellite PM2.5 (global) and the CPCB and OAQ monitoring networks (India). The name combines two Sanskrit words:

- Vayu (वायु) means wind or air.
- Ayan (अयन) means path, journey or movement.

Together, "Vayuayan" means "the path of wind."

## Installation

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
# Install from GitHub
devtools::install_github("saketlab/vayuayan", subdir = "R")
```

## Data sources

The package gives access to three data sources:

1. WUSTL ACAG satellite PM2.5 data from Washington University
   - Global coverage at 0.01 degree (approximately 1 km) resolution
   - Monthly and annual data (1998 to 2024, product V6.GL.03)

2. The CPCB (Central Pollution Control Board) monitoring network in India
   - Historical and real-time AQI data
   - Station-level and city-level data

3. The OAQ (Open Air Quality) low-cost sensor networks in India
   - Many providers, for example Airnet
   - Daily, monthly, and annual data

## Quick start

```{r quickstart, eval = TRUE}
library(vayuayan)
library(dplyr)

vayuayan_welcome()
```

# Historical AQI data

The `cpcb_` functions provide access to historical air quality data from the Central Pollution Control Board.

## Available data

The lists of states, cities and stations come from a CPCB station directory
in the package. Thus, these calls work offline.

```{r historical_explore, eval = TRUE}
states <- cpcb_get_state_list()
head(states)

cities <- cpcb_get_city_list("Maharashtra")
head(cities)

stations <- cpcb_get_station_list("Mumbai")
head(stations)
```

### Station coordinates

```{r add_coords, eval = TRUE}
delhi_stations <- cpcb_add_coords(cpcb_get_station_list("Delhi"))
head(delhi_stations)
```

## Daily data in long format

`cpcb_city_daily()` downloads the CPCB daily file for each city and returns
one row per day. The package caches the files, so later calls read them from
disk.

```{r city_daily}
daily <- cpcb_city_daily(c("Delhi", "Mumbai"), 2024, cache_dir = tempdir())

daily %>%
  group_by(city, month) %>%
  summarise(pm25 = mean(value), .groups = "drop")
```

`cpcb_station_daily()` does the same for stations:

```{r station_daily}
station_daily <- cpcb_station_daily(
  head(delhi_stations$value, 3), 2025,
  cache_dir = tempdir()
)
count(station_daily, station_id)
```

If you want the file itself, `cpcb_download_city_data()` and
`cpcb_download_station_data()` save the raw CPCB sheet.

# Live AQI data

The live readings come from the public station feed. The feed holds only the
latest hour.

```{r live_aqi}
nearest <- cpcb_get_nearest_station(coords = c(19.0760, 72.8777))
nearest

aqi_data <- cpcb_get_live_aqi_data(station_id = nearest$station_id)
aqi_data$metrics
```

Without arguments, `cpcb_get_live_aqi_data()` finds the station nearest to
your IP location.

## Station summaries

`stations_to_dataframe()` flattens the live feed into one row per station,
with an AQI category.

```{r live_table}
live <- stations_to_dataframe(cpcb_get_all_india())

live %>%
  group_by(state_id) %>%
  summarise(
    stations = n(),
    live = sum(live),
    avg_aqi = mean(avg_aqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(stations)) %>%
  head(10)

count(live, aqi_category, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r live_map}
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)

aqi_colors <- c(
  "Good"         = "green",
  "Satisfactory" = "lightgreen",
  "Moderate"     = "yellow",
  "Poor"         = "orange",
  "Very Poor"    = "red",
  "Severe"       = "darkred",
  "No Data"      = "grey70"
)

live %>%
  filter(live) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(color = aqi_category), size = 2, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = aqi_colors) +
  labs(title = "Live CPCB monitoring stations", color = "AQI category") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# PM2.5 satellite data

The `pm25_` functions process satellite PM2.5 data from WUSTL ACAG
(product V6.GL.03 on the AWS Open Data registry). The Asia subset
(`region = "AS"`) includes India, and its file is smaller than the global
file. The package caches the files in `tools::R_user_dir("vayuayan", "cache")`.
The vignette build does not run these chunks.

```{r pm25_setup, eval = FALSE}
pm25_nc <- pm25_download_netcdf(2023, 11, region = "AS")
delhi <- india_boundary(state = "Delhi")
```

## Regional statistics

```{r pm25_stats, eval = FALSE}
pm25_get_stats(
  geojson_file = "https://geo.bharatviz.org/geojsons/cities/delhi.geojson",
  nc_file      = pm25_nc
)

pm25_get_stats(
  geojson_file = "https://geo.bharatviz.org/geojsons/districts/India_LGD_districts.geojson",
  nc_file      = pm25_nc,
  group_by     = "state_name"
)
```

## Maps

```{r pm25_map, eval = FALSE}
r <- pm25_load_netcdf_bbox(pm25_nc, delhi, var = "PM25", mask = TRUE)
pm25_map(r, delhi, title = "Delhi, November 2023")
```

## Cache management

```{r pm25_cache, eval = FALSE}
pm25_list_cached_files()
pm25_clear_cache()
```

# Utility functions

```{r utilities, eval = TRUE}
clean_station_name("Dr. Karni Singh Shooting Range, Delhi - DPCC")

get_aqi_categories(c(42, 180, 320))

# Mumbai to Delhi, in km
haversine_distance(19.0760, 72.8777, 28.7041, 77.1025)
```
